chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When he would pray over a woman and a man, he would place the woman first and delay the man; when he would pray over a slave and a free person, he would place the slave first and delay the free person; and when he would pray over a child and an adult, he would place the child first and delay the adult.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ وَالْحُرُّ: The slave and the free person

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for praying funeral prayers over multiple deceased individuals of different genders and statuses?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the specific protocol for funeral prayers, establishing a hierarchy where women, slaves, and children are placed in front of men, free persons, and adults respectively. While some scholars interpret this as reflecting social status or merit, others view it as a matter of ritual order (tartib) rather than inherent superiority, highlighting the nuanced application of precedence in Shia jurisprudence.
